partners.mechanism_chain: TWIST1 (HGNC:12060) —LEADS_TO→ Robinow-Sorauf syndrome (MONDO:0008391); HMOX1 (HGNC:4788) —DISRUPTS→ Heme degradation pathway (REACT:R-HSA-69974); Heme degradation pathway (REACT:R-HSA-69974) —DECREASES→ Heme (CHEBI:17794); Heme degradation pathway (REACT:R-HSA-69974) —DECREASES→ Biliverdin (CHEBI:17813); Heme degradation pathway (REACT:R-HSA-69974) —DECREASES→ Carbon monoxide (CHEBI:17677); Heme degradation pathway (REACT:R-HSA-69974) —DECREASES→ Iron (CHEBI:29998); HMOX1 (HGNC:4788) —LEADS_TO→ Heme oxygenase 1 deficiency (MONDO:0013536); Heme (CHEBI:17794) —LEADS_TO→ Robinow-Sorauf syndrome (MONDO:0008391). Loss-of-function mutations in TWIST1 cause Robinow-Sorauf syndrome (n1->n2). Loss-of-function mutations in HMOX1 disrupt heme degradation (n3->n5), leading to decreased production of biliverdin, carbon monoxide, and iron (n5->n6, n5->n7, n5->n8), and accumulation of heme (n5->n4). This accumulation of heme, a pro-oxidant molecule, is hypothesized to contribute to the phenotypes observed in Robinow-Sorauf syndrome (n4->n2), creating a mechanistic link between the two diseases.

partners.diseaseBName: Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial diseases due to complete IL12B deficiency
partners.mechanism_chain: TWIST1 (HGNC:12045) —DISRUPTS→ Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (GO:0001837); Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (GO:0001837) —LEADS_TO→ Craniofacial abnormalities (HP:0000252); Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (GO:0001837) —LEADS_TO→ Anhidrosis (HP:0009077); IL12B (HGNC:5530) —DISRUPTS→ Cytokine signaling pathway (GO:0007242); Cytokine signaling pathway (GO:0007242) —LEADS_TO→ Susceptibility to mycobacterial infections (HP:0030060). Loss-of-function mutations in TWIST1 disrupt epithelial-mesenchymal transition, leading to craniofacial abnormalities and anhidrosis characteristic of Robinow-Sorauf syndrome. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in IL12B disrupt the cytokine signaling pathway, specifically impairing IL-12 signaling, which is critical for cell-mediated immunity and leads to Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial diseases. The convergence is on the broader cytokine signaling pathway, where TWIST1's role in regulating inflammatory gene expression can indirectly impact the immune response, creating a shared module of dysregulated immune and developmental signaling.

**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-6785807)

Loss-of-function mutations in TWIST1 cause Robinow-Sorauf syndrome (n1->n2). Loss-of-function mutations in HMOX1 disrupt heme degradation (n3->n5), leading to decreased production of biliverdin, carbon monoxide, and iron (n5->n6, n5->n7, n5->n8), and accumulation of heme (n5->n4). **How to falsify it:** The absence of elevated heme levels or related downstream markers (e.g., oxidative stress markers) in patients with Robinow-Sorauf syndrome, or the presence of pathogenic variants in HMOX1 in Robinow-Sorauf syndrome patients that are not associated with heme oxygenase 1 deficiency. _(variant: rs74305433)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding this link could reveal novel therapeutic targets for Robinow-Sorauf syndrome by modulating heme levels or mitigating heme-induced cellular damage. Conversely, insights from TWIST1 function might inform management of heme-related toxicities in heme oxygenase 1 deficiency.
